name: kvdb.io
tagline: Hosted key-value store driven by plain HTTP calls, with scoped access tokens, TTLs and Lua bucket scripts.
description: kvdb.io, run by Pilvy LLC since 2018, gives you key-value 'buckets' over a REST API: create one with a curl call, then set, get, list by prefix, atomically increment counters and delete keys. Keys are kept in lexicographic order, buckets can have default TTLs, a transaction endpoint applies several sets and deletes together, and short-lived access tokens can be scoped to a key prefix with read or write rights so browser and serverless code never sees the master secret. Lua scripts attached to a bucket run server-side per HTTP request. It suits prototypes, counters, feature flags and small serverless apps; there is a 14-day free trial, a $19/month Pro plan and an Enterprise tier that can run on-premises.

pricing.notes: 14-day free trial; Pro includes 1 GB and 1M ops (+$1/GB, +$5 per million ops); Enterprise $499/month with encryption at rest and on-prem via Docker/Kubernetes.

scale.notes: Sized for small apps and prototypes; storage billed per GB. Internal scaling is not documented.

strengths: Working key-value store from a single curl call, no SDK required
Prefix-scoped, expiring access tokens for safe client-side use
Atomic counters, ordered prefix listing and multi-key transactions
weaknesses: Small single-vendor service with no published SLA on lower tiers
No free tier after the 14-day trial
Limited querying beyond key and prefix access
useCases: Counters and metrics from serverless functions
Feature flags and small config values
